newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar slides after NY specs bale out.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar slides after NY specs bale out.

text.p: London white sugar futures burst into life after a lacklustre morning as speculators finally moved to liquidate hefty net long positions in the New York market, traders said on Friday.

July raws tumbled 27 points to 11.10 cents/lb as speculators made their long-awaited decision to starting baling out of the contract before expiry on June 30 and reduce some of its large open interest.
London took its cue from the sell-off but end-users were quick to buy back August positions at the lows.
"There's an awful lot of buying in the whites. It's following New York but not by anything like the same degree," said one trader.
"It's all end-user buying -- the producers sold the rally and on this dip all the end-users are buying their Augusts back," he said.
At 1510 GMT August, the most heavily traded position, stood $2.30 lower at at intraday low of $321.00. October was down $2.40 at $315.50 and volume amounted to a solid 2,252 lots.
Arbitrage activity was more active than previously in the week although traders said August/July was commanding little interest.
March/March attracted concerted selling at $69.50 and May/May was also valued as a sell, they said.
The Paris market also moved lower but volume stayed on the thin side at just 296 lots. August was down $2.30 at $321.00 and October down $2.50 at $315.50.
